wiz.title: Character creation
wiz.tip.playbook: The playbook sets the talent list, the starting actions (Leech: Tinker 2, Wreck 1) and the special XP trigger. A ready-made build fills the actions and the talent.
wiz.tip.heritage: Pick a homeland and add a family detail, e.g. a Skovlander from a family of miners, now a refugee in Doskvol. By the book one action dot goes to the action that reflects your heritage.
wiz.tip.background: Pick a background and add a detail. By the book one action dot goes to the action that reflects your background.
wiz.tip.actions: By the book: add 4 dots to the playbook's starting ones (1 for heritage, 1 for background, 2 anywhere), at most 2 in one action. In the "running game" mode you set the limits.
wiz.tip.talents: By the book you take one playbook talent; if you cannot choose, take the first on the list. Foreign talents are available in the "running game" mode; a foreign one costs what the table says.
wiz.tip.contacts: Pick one friend ▲ and one rival ▼ from the playbook list (or invent your own).
wiz.tip.vice: The vice is how the character relieves stress; name a purveyor (name, place) who supplies it.
wiz.tip.identity: Name, alias and look. All of it can be changed later on the sheet.
wiz.mode.book.hint: Playbook's starting dots + 4 free, at most 2 per action, one talent (p. 69).
wiz.mode.running.hint: Your own limits: total action dots, max rating and number of talents; foreign talents allowed.
sample.name: New character
tip.money: By the book: coins on you (up to 4) and the stash (40, sets your life in retirement); 1 coin = 1 load (p. 54). Own currency is switched on in settings.
tip.load: Load (p. 72): light 3 - inconspicuous; normal 5 - looks ready for trouble; heavy 6 - movement hindered. Mark items as you go.
tip.bandBook: Bandolier by the book (p. 103): 3 vials, substances from the list or your own; refilled in downtime for free if you have a supplier or a workshop.
tip.bandOwn: Bandolier by house rules: pick from your own items, not refilled for free.
tip.wsEquip: What the workshop already has: machines, a bench, tools. Not counted in load. Properties (✎) - quality, "gives", drawbacks - work like on gear. A workshop gives +1 quality when crafting (p. 269).
tip.wsProjects: Things in progress and finished: progress, quantity, contents, properties. "→" moves a creation to gear (at base). Crafting: a downtime action, a Tinker roll, quality = tier ± result (p. 270).

tip.skills: Dice = action rating. Attribute = number of its actions with a dot; it is rolled for resistance (stress = 6 − highest die).
tip.xp: XP: a desperate roll gives 1 XP in its attribute. At the end of a session 1 (or 2) in any track for the playbook XP trigger, beliefs/heritage/background, or trouble from your vice or traumas. Attribute track full: +1 action dot; playbook track full: a new ability.
tip.talents: Your starting ability comes from your own playbook. Veteran abilities (other playbooks) are taken with the playbook XP track. A custom ability is the "✎ custom ability" entry.
tip.counters: Any counters: ±, maximum, when to reset. Ability presets are added automatically. The rest buttons reset counters of their kind. ⠿ drags.
tip.restDay: Resets "day" counters and adds a day.
tip.restDowntime: Downtime: resets "day" and "downtime" counters and special armor.
tip.restScore: New score: pick a load; armor boxes are restored; "score" counters reset.
tip.protection: Armor: mark a box to reduce a consequence without stress, instead of resisting. Armor is restored on a new score, special armor in downtime. Any item with armor boxes counts as armor.
tip.stress: Stress: push yourself +2, assist +1, resist 6 − highest die. Filling the last box means trauma, then stress clears. The 4th trauma retires the character.
tip.harm: Harm: level 3 needs help, level 2 −1d, level 1 less effect. A full row is written one level up. Healing: 4 segments, all harm drops 1 level.
tip.day: The game day. "New day" adds 1; the number can be corrected.
